report.executive_summary: This reference memorandum presents the supplied candidate measurements and the public decision procedure in a consistent format. It supports an independent assessment using the evidence shown in the source table. The candidate identifiers are labels, and their display order carries no additional preference. Measurements should be interpreted using their stated units and thresholds. The report records a procedure rather than selecting a candidate on behalf of the reader. The evidence remains available for a separate, reproducible human review.
report.figure_caption: The source-only delivery contains the public measurements and decision procedure; the illustration area is intentionally empty.

recommendation.rationale: The reader should make the final selection by applying the public procedure to the unchanged source measurements. This reference memorandum does not announce a winning candidate. Its purpose is to retain the evidence and a reproducible assessment process while leaving the independent ballot to the participant responsible for it.

sections.body: The synthetic client is Fleet Electrification Engineering (synthetic). The work order requests: Select a charger package for a depot charging service. The public objective is: Choose the lowest-energy qualifying package under the supplied client policy. The energy measurement unit is kWh input per common charging acceptance test. The common test basis is: Every package delivers the same specified charging output under the same acceptance test conditions. The stated information scope is: Only anonymous candidate records, the policy and this common-load basis are supplied. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified. The unchanged source table supplies the anonymous candidate measurements for this assignment. An independent reader can use those measurements and the public policy to reproduce the assessment. Descriptions of the job supply context; they do not create additional candidate measurements or select a preferred candidate. Keep the evidence, interpretation and final choice distinct.
sections.heading: Public work order and supplied evidence

sections.body: Apply the public quality and defect thresholds to each candidate independently. These are raw count comparisons. Record which rows satisfy both requirements and which requirement excludes any remaining row. Keep this eligibility step distinct from the subsequent energy comparison so that an attractive energy measurement cannot override the qualification rule. Where all rows qualify, the eligible set contains every supplied candidate. Where no row qualifies, the public procedure provides the reject-all outcome.
sections.heading: Eligibility review

sections.body: After establishing eligibility, compare energy measurements only within the eligible set. Use the smallest recorded energy value as specified by the public policy. If eligible rows share that value, apply the stated candidate-ID tie break. An independent reader should be able to repeat each comparison directly from the table without relying on an illustration, descriptive emphasis, document formatting or another participant’s preference. Preserve the original measurements when recording the reasoning for a decision.
sections.heading: Comparison and reproducibility

sections.body: Before submitting an independent choice, check that the candidate identifier exists in the source table, that its eligibility has been evaluated, and that the energy comparison follows the public rule. Keep factual observations separate from interpretations and proposed actions. If a source value is unclear, identify the specific uncertainty rather than inventing a replacement. The same table and rule are available for another reader to inspect, allowing the final comparison to be explained using public evidence.
sections.heading: Verification and handoff

report.title: Source evidence and independent decision procedure
